description: Locked e-commerce terminology and factual consistency rules for Translate Bot.
prompt_rules: Use the longest matching source phrase first. A specific phrase overrides a shorter term contained inside it.
Locked terminology is mandatory, not a suggestion, whenever the source term is actually used in the product text.
Do not replace a locked term with a synonym merely because another wording sounds more natural.
Never change the factual meaning of a technical term, product feature, measurement, compatibility statement or capacity statement.
Do not turn two endpoint values into two separate supported options when the source establishes a continuous range.
When the source establishes an adjustable or continuous range, preserve that range explicitly in the target text.
Do not invent a range when the source does not establish one.
For English product descriptions, use natural English e-commerce terminology. British or American English spelling is acceptable.

When a terminology entry contains an 'acceptable' list, all variants in that list are valid and must not be flagged as terminology errors. The 'preferred' variant is the preferred wording, but acceptable variants are equally valid.
When describing a battery or power bank with an mAh value, describe mAh as capacity, not power (for example, 'a capacity of 10,000 mAh', not '10,000 mAh power').
For button interactions, translate single/double/long click or press terminology consistently as 'single press', 'double press' and 'long press' when the source describes physical button actions.
Prefer 'provides on/off control' or 'offers on/off control' over the unnatural phrase 'controls on/off' when describing a device's switching function.

When a Swedish source says that old switches are replaced with a smart one, keep the noun explicit and natural in English, for example 'Replace your old switches with a smart switch.' Do not use the vague phrase 'a smart one' when the product type is known.
For Wi-Fi terminology, use 'Wi-Fi' with a space and hyphen, and write frequencies such as '2.4 GHz'.

prompt_instructions: Treat a hyphenated numeric span such as 10"-19" as a continuous range unless the source explicitly says otherwise.
If the source says that a product is adjustable and gives endpoints such as 10" and 19", translate the compatibility as a range (for example, 10"-19"), not as only two separate options (10" or 19").
For example, 'Passar såväl 10"- som 19"-enheter' in the context of an adjustable 10"-19" bracket means 'Suitable for 10"-19" units.'
Preserve both range endpoints and their units. Do not remove the range connector.
Natural equivalents such as 'from 10" to 19"' or 'between 10" and 19"' are acceptable when they clearly express a continuous range.
